# Josupeit.Practices.Jobs.Core

> Abstract base classes for implementing the `Josupeit.Practices.Jobs.Abstractions` job model: `JobBase` holds the identity, the six state flags, `Exception`, the `Changed` event, a `CancellationToken` that `Cancel()` signals, the guards `ThrowIfCannotStart()`/`ThrowIfCannotCancel()`, and the protected transitions `NotifyPending()`, `NotifyExecuting()`, `NotifyFailed(Exception)`, `NotifyCanceled()`. The four classes you derive from - `Job`, `JobWithResult<TResult>`, `JobWithProgress<TProgress>`, `JobWithProgressAndResult<TProgress, TResult>` - implement the matching interfaces and add `NotifySucceeded(...)` and, for progress, `NotifyProgress(TProgress?)`. You implement `Start()`. `JobBase` itself does not implement `IJob`. Targets netstandard2.0 and net8.0; depends only on the Abstractions package; lives in the `Josupeit.Practices.Jobs` namespace.

Install with `dotnet add package Josupeit.Practices.Jobs.Core`. All types live in the `Josupeit.Practices.Jobs` namespace - not `Josupeit.Practices.Jobs.Core`. Types:

- `JobBase` - abstract; `Id`, `Exception`, `IsPending`/`IsExecuting`/`IsCompleted`/`IsCompletedSuccessfully`/`IsFaulted`/`IsCanceled`, `event Changed`, protected `CancellationToken`, `abstract Start()`, `virtual Cancel()`, `protected virtual OnChanged()`, protected `NotifyPending()`/`NotifyExecuting()`/`NotifyFailed(Exception)`/`NotifyCanceled()`, protected `ThrowIfCannotStart()`/`ThrowIfCannotCancel()`; does **not** implement `IJob`
- `Job : JobBase, IJob` - adds protected `NotifySucceeded()`
- `JobWithResult<TResult>` - adds `TResult? Result` and protected `NotifySucceeded(TResult? result)`
- `JobWithProgress<TProgress>` - adds `TProgress? Progress`, protected `NotifyProgress(TProgress?)`, protected `NotifySucceeded()`
- `JobWithProgressAndResult<TProgress, TResult>` - both

All constructors are protected and parameterless; flag setters are `private` or `private protected`, so state changes only through `Notify*`, each of which raises `Changed`. `Notify*` does not validate order; your `Start` must end every path in exactly one terminal call. `ThrowIfCannotStart()` throws `InvalidOperationException` when pending, executing, or completed; keep `Start()` synchronous up to the guard (an `async void Start()` turns that exception into a process-terminating unhandled one). `Cancel()` throws after completion, is idempotent, and signals the token on a thread-pool thread without transitioning the job.

## Documentation

- [Complete reference](https://codeberg.org/DerPeit/Josupeit.Practices/raw/branch/main/src/Josupeit.Practices.Jobs/llms-full.txt): the transitions table, guards, cancellation semantics, `OnChanged`, declarations, four complete jobs (delegate, result and progress, external engine, UI marshaling), a factory skeleton, and common mistakes. Load this to write code against the package.
- [PublicAPI.Shipped.txt](https://codeberg.org/DerPeit/Josupeit.Practices/raw/branch/main/src/Josupeit.Practices.Jobs/PublicAPI.Shipped.txt): analyzer-enforced inventory of every public and protected member. `!` marks non-nullable and `?` nullable reference types; accessibility is not shown.
- [README](https://codeberg.org/DerPeit/Josupeit.Practices/raw/branch/main/src/Josupeit.Practices.Jobs/README.md): human-oriented package overview as shown on NuGet.
